aspects.says: StringBuffer makes each method call atomic, so a line written with several calls to a shared buffer can be interleaved with another thread's; building the line locally and appending it in one call keeps it whole.
basis: section:StringBuffer Locks Each Call, So a Line Built from Several Calls Still Interleaves

aspects.says: Where several calls on a shared object must stay together, the text is built before the lock is taken, so a slow part of one record doesn't hold up the other threads.
basis: section:StringBuffer Locks Each Call, So a Line Built from Several Calls Still Interleaves

aspects.says: StringBuilder and StringBuffer inherit equals and hashCode from Object, so two builders with the same text are different set entries; content is compared with compareTo, contentEquals or toString().
basis: section:Two Builders Are Equal Only When They Are the Same Object

aspects.says: A builder that runs out of room grows to the larger of what is needed and twice its capacity plus 2 by copying, so appending stays linear and sizing it to the result avoids the growth garbage.
basis: section:A Builder Is an Array: Growing It and Inserting at the Front Copy What Is Already There

aspects.says: insert at the front shifts every character already in the builder on every call, so a loop of front inserts takes time that grows with the square of the count.
basis: section:A Builder Is an Array: Growing It and Inserting at the Front Copy What Is Already There

aspects.says: Reusing a builder for short lines saved no allocation in the measured run, because the JIT can remove a fresh builder's allocation.
basis: section:setLength(0) Empties a Builder and Keeps Its Array
aspects.reason: what the JIT removes, and the time per line, vary by JVM and flags; a graded test cannot assert them deterministically, and the page hedges the measurement

aspects.says: A check of a StringBuffer followed by an append is two locked calls, so another thread can act between them.
basis: section:StringBuffer Locks Each Call, So a Line Built from Several Calls Still Interleaves

aspects.says: setLength(0) empties a builder but keeps its array, so a reused builder holds its largest size; trimToSize() gives it back but leaves no room.
basis: section:setLength(0) Empties a Builder and Keeps Its Array

aspects.says: One StringBuilder shared between threads, even a scratch builder cleared before each use, mixes or loses their text, and can throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
basis: section:StringBuffer Locks Each Call, So a Line Built from Several Calls Still Interleaves

aspects.says: After warm-up the JIT may merge adjacent locks on the same buffer, so a test that passes then proves nothing about the code.
basis: section:StringBuffer Locks Each Call, So a Line Built from Several Calls Still Interleaves
aspects.reason: whether the JIT coarsens the locks depends on compilation state and JVM flags, which a deterministic graded test cannot control; the page shows both runs
